segments.flavor: station ID, the hour opens climbing
segments.text: Tess: [cheerful] Hitline. Ten songs an hour, every one of them climbing. Number one starts now.

segments.flavor: station ID, the signature sign-off
segments.text:
Tess: Hitline. Where the chart only goes one direction, and that direction is up.
Tess: And that's number one. Go!

segments.flavor: station ID, everything here is counted
segments.text:
Tess: You found Hitline. Everything here is counted, and everything counted is rising.
Tess: Volume up. Here it comes.

segments.flavor: station ID, the fastest chart in the world
segments.text:
Tess: [shouting] HITLINE! Fastest chart in the world, and it is still getting faster.
Tess: Count with me. One, and play it.

segments.flavor: Tess counts three unrelated things about her day and ends on 'and that's number one'
segments.text:
Tess: Buttons on this jacket, six. Umbrellas lost this month, three. Songs I loved today, all of them.
Tess: That is three counts, one jacket, and that is number one. Play it.

segments.flavor: Tess counts three unrelated things about her day and ends on 'and that's number one'
segments.text:
Tess: Elevator rides today, nine. Floors I actually wanted, two. Choruses I sang in there, all nine.
Tess: Nine out of nine singing, and that is number one. Here we go.

segments.flavor: Tess counts three unrelated things about her day and ends on 'and that's number one'
segments.text:
Tess: Three counts before the next song. Socks matching, zero. Keys found, one. Ideas, forty.
Milo: Forty ideas is up eleven percent on your own average, which I keep.
Tess: You keep an average of my ideas?
Milo: Column R. It updates itself. And right now, column R is trending.
Tess: Then column R can take the bow, and that is number one. Roll it.

segments.flavor: Tess counts three unrelated things about her day and ends on 'and that's number one'
segments.text:
Tess: Counting the day so far. Doors I pushed that said pull, four.
Milo: Four is high. The national figure is one point two doors.
Tess: Sandwiches eaten standing up, two. Both of them over this desk.
Milo: The desk is now the third most crumbed surface in this building.
Tess: And songs that made me forget every one of those doors, all of them.
Milo: That is still not a countable quantity, and I have tried to count it.
Tess: It is here, and that is number one. Music, please.

segments.flavor: Milo cites an invented chart statistic with total confidence and one absurd demographic
segments.text:
Milo: This next one is up sixty percent among people who own a ladder.
Tess: A ladder. That is the demographic.
Milo: One ladder. Two ladders is a different chart entirely. Here it climbs.

segments.flavor: Milo cites an invented chart statistic with total confidence and one absurd demographic
segments.text:
Milo: Hitline fact. This song tests forty-one percent stronger with anyone currently holding a mug.
Tess: Holding a mug. Not drinking from it.
Milo: Drinking from it drops you to nineteen. The mug is the variable, not the tea.
Tess: Mugs down, everyone. I want the honest number. Song, now!

segments.flavor: Milo cites an invented chart statistic with total confidence and one absurd demographic
segments.text:
Milo: New data. This one performs eighty-eight percent better in rooms with one window.
Tess: One window. What happens in a room with two?
Milo: It collapses. Two windows and the song tests worse than silence.
Tess: So the whole chart depends on somebody's builder.
Milo: The builders are eleven percent of my sample and they refuse to answer.
Tess: Then we go with one window. Windows closed, volume up!

segments.flavor: Milo cites an invented chart statistic with total confidence and one absurd demographic
segments.text:
Milo: I ran the numbers again and then I ran them a third time.
Tess: [sarcastic] That is two times, Milo. Three is a different word.
Milo: This next track is up seventy-two percent among people who have named their car.
Tess: Named their car. As in given it a name.
Milo: A first name only. Full names drop it to thirty-one percent. Nicknames, unreadable.
Tess: Why would a surname hurt a song?
Milo: Formality. A car with a surname never dances. That is in the notes.
Tess: You keep notes about whether cars dance.
Milo: I have a tab. It is colour coded and it is climbing.
Tess: Then start the engine, whatever its name is, and drive into this one!

segments.flavor: a fake ad for a phone plan, an energy bar or a music festival, sincere announcer grammar, rapid disclaimer from Milo
segments.text:
Tess: Hitline runs on Nimbus Mobile. One plan, one price, one small footnote.
Milo: The footnote is four pages. Page three is just the word sorry.
Tess: Nimbus Mobile. Ring us later. Music now!

segments.flavor: a fake ad for a phone plan, an energy bar or a music festival, sincere announcer grammar, rapid disclaimer from Milo
segments.text:
Tess: Chorus Crunch. The energy bar with a key change inside.
Milo: Bar contains no key change. The middle is caramel and regret.
Tess: One bar, one chorus, and the day gets loud again.
Milo: Chew responsibly. Ninety percent of testers chewed in time. Terms chewy.
Tess: Chorus Crunch. Back to the climb!

segments.flavor: a fake ad for an energy bar shaped like a sound wave
segments.text:
Tess: Thrum. The energy bar shaped like a sound wave and priced like a snack.
Milo: Thrum contains oats, honey, and an ingredient listed only as more.
Tess: One Thrum before the last hour and the last hour becomes the first hour.
Milo: Time does not reverse. Thrum makes no claim about time. Thrum is a bar.
Tess: Thrum. Chew loud. Now the music!

segments.flavor: a fake ad for a festival with a scheduled sunrise
segments.text:
Tess: Loudfield. One weekend, one valley, and a sunrise that arrives with a bassline.
Milo: The sunrise is not scheduled by us. We schedule everything except the sunrise.
Tess: Sixty acts across five stages, and the smallest stage always wins the weekend.
Milo: Smallest stage holds two hundred. Everyone else watches the biggest stage. Statistically.
Tess: Loudfield. Bring your voice. You will leave without it.
Milo: [serious] Voice loss is common, expected, and not covered by the ticket.
Tess: Worth it. Every time. Back to the songs!

segments.flavor: a fake ad for a phone plan sold with one bar of signal
segments.text:
Tess: Halo Mobile. A phone plan with one bar of signal and infinite confidence.
Milo: One bar is the plan. Two bars costs extra and is called Halo Plus.
Tess: Calls, texts, and a little ring of light around your name.
Milo: The ring of light is a sticker. It is on the box. Terms apply.
Tess: Halo Mobile. Shine on. Let it play!

segments.flavor: The Plant Report, the studio plant that is trending
segments.text:
Tess: Time for the Plant Report. Milo, how is the studio plant doing this week?
Milo: The plant is up. It is always up. This week it is up thirteen percent.
Tess: Up in what sense? It has one leaf and no opinions.
Milo: Two leaves. And it charts. Everyone who walks past it looks at it.
Tess: That is not charting, that is a plant in a corridor.
Milo: A plant in a corridor with a thirteen percent look rate is a hit.
Tess: Then congratulations to the plant. Water it on the way past.
Milo: It is already the third most photographed thing in this building.
Tess: Beaten only by the desk and the crumbs. Play on!

segments.flavor: The Spreadsheet, Milo ranks the week's feelings
segments.text:
Tess: It is time for the spreadsheet. Milo keeps a spreadsheet of feelings.
Milo: Of all feelings. Sorted, dated, and colour coded. This week has a clear winner.
Tess: Give me the winning feeling.
Milo: The winning feeling is the one just before a chorus. Column C. Deep orange.
Tess: What is in second place?
Milo: The feeling when a song you forgot comes on in a shop. Pale green.
Tess: Pale green is beautiful. What is last?
Milo: Last is waiting for a song to load. Grey. Always grey. Never moves.
Tess: Nothing loads here. Deep orange, right now!

segments.flavor: The Wrong Count, an audit of Milo's errors
segments.text:
Tess: The Wrong Count. Milo, how many times have you been wrong since we started?
Milo: Zero. The count is zero. It has always been zero.
Tess: I have fourteen on my hand. I wrote them on my hand.
Milo: A hand is not a source. Sources need a date and a signature.
Tess: I signed it. I signed my own hand, Milo.
Milo: Then that is one source and one hand and no independent audit.
Tess: Number fifteen, right there, live.
Milo: You cannot count a disagreement as a wrong. That is the rule.
Tess: I make the rules, I make the counts, and I make this song start now.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for a phone plan, an energy bar or a music festival, sincere announcer grammar, rapid disclaimer from Milo
segments.text:
Tess: Three days. One field. Big Field Weekend, and the sky is part of the ticket.
Milo: Sky not included. The sky is weather, and weather is not our partner.
Tess: Forty acts. Four stages. One enormous chorus that you will hear from the road.
Milo: Road not included either. Parking is the same field, sold twice.
Tess: Bring a coat you love and shoes you can forgive.
Milo: Tickets are final. Weather is final. Your shoes are entirely your business.
Tess: Big Field Weekend. Get in the field. Here comes the chorus!

segments.flavor: a fake ad for a phone plan, an energy bar or a music festival, sincere announcer grammar, rapid disclaimer from Milo
segments.text:
Tess: Something new. Toneline. A fresh ringtone every week, delivered while you sleep.
Milo: Delivered is a strong word. It arrives. Sometimes it arrives at four.
Tess: Fifty-two ringtones a year. One for every mood you have ever had on a phone.
Milo: Testing found people have six moods on a phone. Toneline sends fifty-two anyway.
Tess: Your phone rings and the room turns around. That is the promise.
Milo: The room might turn around for someone else's phone. Toneline accepts no responsibility.
Tess: Cancel any time, they say, and I believe them.
Milo: Cancelling is a form. The form is a ringtone. Play it to cancel.
Tess: Toneline. Let it ring, then let this one play!

segments.flavor: back-announce {STREAM} as this week's biggest climber; Milo gives the percentage
segments.text:
Tess: That was Paper Rockets with Slow Down The Sun, this week's biggest climber.
Milo: Up thirty-four places. Steepest move our board has recorded.
Tess: They were nowhere. Now the graph is a wall.
Milo: It is a wall. Walls are up eight percent this week.
Tess: Keep climbing, Paper Rockets. Here comes the next one!

segments.flavor: back-announce {STREAM} as this week's biggest climber; Milo gives the percentage
segments.text:
Tess: Biggest climber of the week, Hollow Neon with Tin Heart Parade.
Milo: Up twenty-two places, and up sixty-one percent among people who whistle.
Tess: People who whistle are a demographic now?
Milo: A strong group. Quiet, loyal, and they request nothing.
Tess: No requests at all. We should hire them.
Milo: They whistle nine percent above tempo. Their only flaw.
Tess: Nine percent fast, and still loyal. Whistle along with this one!

segments.flavor: back-announce {STREAM} as this week's biggest climber; Milo gives the percentage
segments.text:
Tess: Back-announcing the biggest climber on the board. Cold Arcade, with Half A Mile Of You.
Milo: Up nineteen places. And up forty-four percent among people who cut their own hair.
Tess: That is very specific for a song about walking.
Milo: The song is about walking. The haircut is about confidence. Both are climbing.
Tess: So the chart is measuring confidence now.
Milo: The chart has always measured confidence. I just finally found the column.
Tess: Cold Arcade, halfway up and still walking. Next one now!

segments.flavor: back-announce {STREAM} as this week's biggest climber; Milo gives the percentage
segments.text:
Tess: That climb you just heard belongs to Marble Youth and Ninety Windows.
Milo: Up forty-one places. The biggest single jump this board has ever printed.
Tess: Forty-one places in one week. How does a song do that?
Milo: Three ways. Someone sings it at work. Someone else asks what it is.
Tess: And the third way?
Milo: The third way is a stairwell. Stairwells add eleven percent. Always have.
Tess: You are telling me stairwells make hits.
Milo: Stairwells and lifts. Lifts are worth four. A stairwell is worth eleven.
Tess: Then take the stairs tomorrow and thank Marble Youth.
Milo: I will take the stairs. I will also count them.
Tess: Count away. Ninety Windows, one more time, right now!

segments.flavor: Pippa calls to request the same song again; the song is never named; she never gets it
segments.text:
Tess: Phones are lit, and one of them is Pippa. Pippa, hello!
Pippa: Hello Tess. You know the one I want.
Tess: I looked for it, Pippa. I looked twice.
Pippa: [gentle] Look between the other ones. It hides.
Milo: Nothing hides in a chart. Here is something real instead.

segments.flavor: Pippa calls to request the same song again; the song is never named; she never gets it
segments.text:
Tess: Line one is glowing and I know that voice. Go ahead, Pippa.
Pippa: You know why I am calling. It has been a while.
Milo: Four calls. I log them. Four calls, zero plays.
Pippa: Then the fifth is the lucky one. Put it on, Tess.
Tess: Not this hour, Pippa. Keep believing though.
Milo: Belief is up nine percent. So is this next song. Hear it!

segments.flavor: Pippa calls to request the same song again; the song is never named; she never gets it
segments.text:
Tess: Pippa is back. Pippa, you have thirty seconds and my full attention.
Pippa: I only need six. Same request. You know the one.
Tess: I do. I have known it for a long time now.
Milo: For the record, the song she wants has no chart position at all.
Pippa: It has a position in my head. Very high. Right at the top.
Milo: That is a sample of one. Statistically that is a rumour.
Pippa: [sad] Then play the rumour.
Tess: Next time, Pippa. This one now!

segments.flavor: Pippa calls to request the same song again; the song is never named; she never gets it
segments.text:
Tess: Last phone call before the music. Pippa, I saw your name and smiled.
Pippa: Then you know what happens next. I would like my song.
Tess: Your song. The one you have never once described to me.
Pippa: I should not have to describe it. You already know it.
Milo: I have searched every catalogue we hold, twice, and found nothing at all.
Tess: He really did search. He made a chart of the searching.
Milo: Nine hours of searching. Down two percent on my previous searching.
Pippa: Then search slower. It is a slow song.
Tess: A clue! Milo, write that down. Slow.
Milo: Slow narrows it to nine thousand. Not enough, Pippa.
Tess: Next time we get two clues. Until then, this one plays!

segments.flavor: a fake ad for gum that extends a chorus
segments.text:
Tess: Encore. The gum that keeps a chorus going after the song has finished.
Milo: Chorus not included. Encore includes gum. The chorus is entirely your own work.
Tess: Twelve pieces a pack. Twelve encores. One very busy jaw.
Milo: Chewing for twelve encores takes ninety minutes. Consult nobody. Just stop eventually.
Tess: Encore, encore. And now, the next one!

segments.flavor: a fake ad for a monthly box of things a stage has touched
segments.text:
Tess: The Backstage Box arrives every month with things a stage has touched.
Milo: Touched is broad. A stage touches the floor. The floor is in the box.
Tess: A poster, a wristband, and a letter from someone who was definitely there.
Milo: The letter is printed. Someone was there when the printer was on.
Tess: Open it slowly. That is the whole point of a box.
Milo: Boxes are up six percent among people who open things slowly.
Tess: The Backstage Box. Now, back to the stage!

segments.flavor: a fake ad for a wristband that lights up on the beat
segments.text:
Tess: Sparkline Bands. A wristband that lights up on the beat, and only the beat.
Milo: It lights on any beat. Including your heart. Especially during the quiet songs.
Tess: Put ten thousand of them in a field and the field becomes a chorus.
Milo: Field not included. Band glows for nine hours then glows differently for one.
Tess: Sparkline. Wear the light. Music!

segments.flavor: a fake ad for sparkling water measured in bubbles
segments.text:
Tess: Topline. Sparkling water with the exact amount of sparkle a number one deserves.
Milo: Sparkle is measured in bubbles. Topline contains bubbles. That is the measurement.
Tess: Cold, loud, and gone in four seconds, like the best chorus of your life.
Milo: Four seconds is the record. The average is eleven. Do not race it.
Tess: Topline. Pour it up. Here comes the next climb!

segments.flavor: a fake ad for an app that lends you a stadium echo
segments.text:
Tess: Bigroom. The app that turns any small room into a very large room.
Milo: The room does not change size. The app changes the echo. The echo lies.
Tess: Sing into your phone and hear yourself in a stadium with forty thousand friends.
Milo: The forty thousand are a recording. They cheer for everyone. They cheered for me.
Tess: Even Milo got cheered. That is the technology working.
Milo: It is a loop of applause. It is a good loop. Terms apply.
Tess: Bigroom. Make it enormous. Sing along!

segments.flavor: The Number Two, an hourly pause for the song that just missed
segments.text:
Tess: Every hour we pause for the song at number two. Milo, who is it?
Milo: Wax Harbour, with Tell Me Twice. Two places off the top. Again.
Tess: Number two is the hardest place in the world to stand.
Milo: It is also the safest. Number two has never been dropped by anybody.
Tess: That is a cold way to comfort a band, Milo.
Milo: It is a warm number. Ninety-one percent of number twos are loved more.
Tess: Loved more but played less. That is a sad chart.
Milo: Every chart is a sad chart if you read down the page.
Tess: Then we read upward. Up we go!

segments.flavor: The Countdown, which never quite reaches zero
segments.text:
Tess: Countdown to the next song. Ten. Nine. Eight.
Milo: You skipped nothing yet. I am watching.
Tess: Seven. Six. Five and a half. Five and a quarter.
Milo: That is not how counting works, and I count for a living.
Tess: Four. Three. Three again, because I liked it.
Milo: You cannot like a number back into existence.
Tess: Two. One. And a tiny half after the one.
Milo: There is no half after one. One is the end. Zero is the end.
Tess: [laughing] Zero is for people who stop. Here is the song!

segments.flavor: Chart Court, where Milo prosecutes a song for climbing too fast
segments.text:
Tess: Chart Court is in session. Milo, read the charge.
Milo: The song Iron Lantern is accused of climbing too fast. Eleven places overnight.
Tess: Climbing fast is not a crime. That is the entire job.
Milo: It is suspicious. Nothing honest moves eleven places while people sleep.
Tess: Maybe people were awake. People are awake at strange hours.
Milo: Forty percent of the climb happened between three and four. Explain that.
Tess: Somebody could not sleep and pressed play. Court finds that beautiful.
Milo: The court is one person and she likes the song.
Tess: Case dismissed. Play the evidence!

segments.flavor: One Word Reviews, converted into a percentage
segments.text:
Tess: One Word Reviews. I give the song one word. Milo turns it into a number.
Milo: I do. The word goes in, the percentage comes out. Ready.
Tess: That last one. My word is enormous.
Milo: Enormous scores eighty-eight. It is the fourth strongest word you have ever used.
Tess: What beat it?
Milo: Unstoppable, glittering, and once, memorably, the word yes.
Tess: Yes was a good review. Short and completely honest.
Milo: Yes tested at ninety-six. Nothing has beaten yes.
Tess: Then the next one has to earn a yes. Let us hear it!

segments.flavor: Two Truths and a Chart, where every fact turns out invented
segments.text:
Tess: Two Truths and a Chart. Milo gives me three facts. One is invented.
Milo: Fact one. The average song is played first in a kitchen.
Tess: Plausible. Keep going.
Milo: Fact two. People sing louder with wet hair. Ninety-one percent louder.
Tess: Also plausible, sadly. And the third?
Milo: Fact three. Every hit has a door in it somewhere.
Tess: A door. In the song.
Milo: In the lyric, the video, or the studio. There is always a door.
Tess: I am saying the door one is invented.
Milo: All three were invented. That is the game. I never said otherwise.
Tess: You absolutely did. Play something with a door in it!
